identity.title: Dust Production and Particle Acceleration in Supernova 1987A Revealed with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: In 2012 we used the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array to observe SN 1987A, one of the best-observed supernovae since the invention of the telescope.

evidence.quote: Supernova (SN) 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud was the closest supernova explosion to Earth (50kpc)

question.value: Where does the far-infrared/submillimeter emission of SN 1987A originate, and was the large dust mass formed in the inner ejecta; what is the spectrum of the shock-accelerated torus emission?

evidence.quote: Resolved observations of SN$\,$1987A in the submillimeter regime are required to establish the location of the emission measured by Herschel.

claims.hypothesis: Herschel-detected dust formed in the inner ejecta
claims.experiment: Resolved ALMA images at 450 um-2.8 mm with torus subtraction
claims.result: Ejecta emission compact, rising steeply with frequency, fit by 0.23 Msun carbon dust at 26 K
claims.finding: Large dust mass formed in the inner ejecta, not yet processed by reverse shock

evidence.quote: For the first time we show unambiguously that this dust has formed in the inner ejecta

claims.finding: Shock modified by accelerated particles or amplified field

evidence.quote: The shock structure is therefore likely being modified by pressure from the accelerated particles

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pulsar wind nebula emission rejected for the ejecta spectrum

evidence.quote: The spectrum of the inner ejecta rises steeply with frequency, inconsistent with PWN emission, but very well modeled by dust.

limitations_admitted.value: Silicate dust mass not strongly constrained

evidence.quote: Although these data do not strongly constrain the mass of silicate dust

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust mass depends on assumed opacity and composition
Fit procedure and degeneracies not documented

reproducibility.score_reason: Project code given but imaging and fitting details sparse.
